_comment: Definitions surfaced as inline tooltips. Terms must be used verbatim in UI copy. See docs/GLOSSARY.md.
day_of_coordinator: Someone who handles final-weeks logistics and runs the wedding day itself. Cheaper than a full planner, and the most common choice.
venue_coordinator: Works for the venue, not for you. They make sure the venue's obligations happen, not that your whole day does.
officiant: The person who legally performs the ceremony. Their credentials have to be valid in the state where you marry.
point_person: The friend or family member vendors call on the day so nobody calls you.
save_the_date: An early heads-up sent 6 to 12 months out so guests can book travel. Not the invitation.
invitation_suite: The full mailed set: invitation, RSVP card, details card, envelopes.
response_deadline: The date RSVPs are due, usually 3 to 4 weeks before the wedding so you can give the caterer a final headcount.
escort_card: Tells a guest which table they're at.
place_card: Tells a guest which seat is theirs.
plus_one: A guest's guest. Whether to offer one is a budget decision as much as a social one.
first_look: A private moment where you see each other before the ceremony. It buys back an hour of photo time.
cocktail_hour: The hour between ceremony and reception, usually while you're taking photos.
send_off: The exit at the end of the night: sparklers, bubbles, or a getaway car.
rehearsal_dinner: Dinner the night before, after walking through the ceremony. Traditionally hosted by the groom's family, though that's loosening.
coi: Certificate of insurance. Most venues require your vendors to carry liability coverage and name the venue on the certificate.
force_majeure: The contract clause covering events outside anyone's control. Read this one.
retainer: The deposit that reserves a vendor's date. Usually non-refundable.
service_charge: A mandatory fee, often 20 to 25%, that is not a tip and usually does not go to the staff.
gratuity: The actual tip. Budget for it separately from the service charge.
corkage_fee: What a venue charges to serve wine you supplied.
cake_cutting_fee: What a venue charges per slice to cut and serve a cake you didn't buy from them.
fb_minimum: Food and beverage minimum. The amount you must spend on food and drink, separate from the site fee.
final_headcount: The guest number you commit to, usually 7 to 10 days out. You pay for it whether they come or not.
overtime_rate: The hourly rate if the party runs past contracted end time. Agree on it in advance.
vendor_meal: A meal you're contractually required to feed to photographers, the band, and the planner.
plated: Servers bring each guest a chosen dish. Most formal, needs meal choices collected in advance.
buffet: Guests serve themselves from stations. Usually cheaper, needs more floor space.
family_style: Large shared platters on each table. Feels generous, costs closer to plated.
consumption_bar: You pay for what's actually poured, tallied at the end.
cash_bar: Guests pay for their own drinks. Widely considered poor form in the US.
tablescape: The full look of a set table: linens, centerpiece, chargers, glassware.
sweetheart_table: A table for just the two of you, instead of a head table with the wedding party.
installation: A large floral or decor piece, like a hanging arrangement or a full arch.
uplighting: Lights placed on the floor pointing up walls. The cheapest way to change how a room feels.
run_of_show: The minute-by-minute schedule for the wedding day, shared with every vendor.
shot_list: The specific photos you want. Give it to your photographer at least two weeks out.
golden_hour: The hour before sunset, when outdoor photos look best. Plan the timeline around it.
alterations: Fitting a gown to your body. Takes 6 to 8 weeks and 2 to 3 appointments. This is the single most underestimated lead time in wedding planning.
bustle: The set of hooks or ties that lifts a train off the floor for the reception. Added during alterations, and someone needs to be taught how to do it.
silhouette: The overall shape of a gown: A-line, ball gown, mermaid, sheath.
elopement: Marrying with few or no guests, by choice.
micro_wedding: A full wedding at small scale, usually 50 guests or fewer.
unplugged_ceremony: Guests are asked to put phones away so your photographer gets clean shots.
content_creator: A newer vendor category: someone capturing phone-shot video for social, alongside your photographer.
marriage_license: The legal permit to marry, issued by a county clerk. Distinct from the marriage certificate you get afterward.
waiting_period: Time you must wait between getting the license and using it. Set by state law, and it cannot be waived by planning harder.
name_change: Not automatic. Order matters: Social Security first, then driver's license, then passport, then banks.
